title: Goldsboro revisited: the report and the facts
summary: Quotes page 127 of Ralph Lapp's book "Kill and Overkill": a B-52 jettisoned a 24-megaton bomb over North Carolina and five of six interlocks were set off by the fall. A facing column of "facts" replies: it was an accident, the aircraft broke up, the bomb had four safety devices, not six, and only one switch held. Parts are redacted.

title: Conclusions on the Mk 39 Mod 2 bomb
summary: Lapp's report lacks accuracy, but its central point stands: one low-voltage switch stood between the United States and a major catastrophe. The Mk 39 Mod 2 bomb lacked adequate safety for B-52 airborne alert; Alt 197 added little, and the ready-safe switch was the only effective safing device. A short to an arm line could have caused a nuclear burst.
